title: Engram is a sampler that turns broken AI hallucinations into music
snippet: Music startup Thoughtful Things has just launched the Kickstarter campaign for its first instrument, Engram. It's a sampler and groovebox that uses AI to mangle incoming audio and even hallucinate completely new sounds. This isn't Suno in a box, though. This isn't a "push-button, get-song" device, aimed at creating something that sounds ready for top-40 radio. It's about creating experimental, uncanny sounds and pushing AI audio models beyond their limits. Engram isn't connected to the internet.

title: Column: For physical AI, maps are turning into memory
snippet: A robot that can map a factory floor still cannot necessarily find the box it has been asked to move, or remember what it saw on its last visit. For autonomous robots, building the map is increasingly just the beginning. What comes next — searching for objects, navigating to specified locations, remembering what the robot has seen, and retrieving that information for model reasoning in complex environments — is where the new applications and challenges lie.

title: South Korea's HBM-linked exports surge as Taiwan, Malaysia emerge as high-value destinations
snippet: South Korea's exports of the customs category that carries high-bandwidth memory (HBM) are no longer a two-destination story. Unit-value data show that the chips going to Taiwan and Malaysia are worth several times more per kilogram than those shipped to Hong Kong, China, or Vietnam. That points to a two-tier trade, with premium stacked memory heading to advanced packaging lines and cheaper multichip parts going to transit hubs and lower-unit-value destinations.

title: Weekly news roundup: China gains ground in memory and AI hardware as supply stays tight
snippet: China's AI sector is shifting from catch-up to commercialization, with value concentrating in hardware bottlenecks and large platforms rather than independent model labs. Across memory, DRAM and NAND shortages, HBM reallocation and rising Chinese capacity are reshaping pricing and share gains for CXMT and YMTC. Taiwan and Singapore are extending into glass packaging, photonics and advanced packaging, while Chinese auto ambitions are stirring US backlash ahead of Xi's visit.

title: Apple keeps iPhone Duo in China, exposing limits of India's phone supply chain
snippet: Apple's first foldable iPhone has become a test of how far India has come as a manufacturing base, and the answer is sobering. As India-assembled iPhones reach record export levels, Apple kept development and assembly of its most complex phone, the iPhone Duo, in China. The decision points to a gap that Pune Times Mirror summed up this way: India has become indispensable to Apple's assembly operations, but not yet to its engineering.

title: Column: For physical AI, maps are turning into memory
snippet: A robot that can map a factory floor still cannot necessarily find the box it has been asked to move, or remember what it saw on its last visit. What comes next — searching for objects, navigating to specified locations, remembering what the robot has seen, and retrieving that information for model reasoning in complex environments — is where the new applications and challenges lie.

title: South Korea's HBM-linked exports surge as Taiwan, Malaysia emerge as high-value destinations
snippet: South Korea's exports of the customs category that carries high-bandwidth memory (HBM) are no longer a two-destination story. Unit-value data show that the chips going to Taiwan and Malaysia are worth several times more per kilogram than those shipped to Hong Kong, China, or Vietnam. That points to a two-tier trade, with premium stacked memory heading to advanced packaging lines and cheaper multichip parts going to transit hubs and lower-unit-value destinations.
